text:
alex: FYI noticed a small host-side CPU regression after yesterday's proto change, ~+6% on 50-token p50. @jordan can you sanity-check?

jordan: saw that on dashboards too. traces show more time in parse/dispatch. suspect extra copy in the new frame header path. :thinking_face:

ria: grabbed a quick pprof sample from a heavy host:```
pprof top
flat  cum   function
10ms  30ms host::parse_frame
7ms   25ms host::tokenize
4ms   15ms http2::decode_and_unwrap
3ms   10ms grpc::unmarshal
```

tobias: interesting — parse_frame up 3.5ms vs baseline. Could be the extra length-check we added. I also see more writev syscalls in the flows:```
# strace snippet
writev(4, [{iov_base="...", iov_len=128}, {iov_base="...", iov_len=256}], 2) = 384
writev(4, ... ) = 64
```

alex: writev churn would explain small p50, yes. Are these coming from streaming chunking changes or earlier tokenization split?

jordan: timeline: tokenization refactor landed Mon, proto header change landed Tue. Traces that include both show extra framing path when requests are small and use grpc stream multiplexing.

ria: I ran a microbench isolating tokenization vs parse. Tokenize went from 0.9ms -> 1.2ms (50-token). Parse_frame from 1.6ms -> 3.1ms. So parse is dominant.

alex: good data. For next steps: (1) toggle the new proto header fast-path to confirm, (2) instrument the frame copy site to see if we can avoid allocation/copy, (3) run a kvcache-aware batch test to ensure we didn't regress cache hit tail.

jordan: toggled flag on staging: deploy-bot: started deploy rev 9c3b to staging (flag:proto_fastpath=false)
deploy-bot: deploy finished in 18s, rolling pods ready

ria: with flag off p50 back to baseline, host CPU diff goes away. So it's the header path.

tobias: root cause: we introduced a temporary buffer to normalize headers, then memcpy into iov list. For small frames the memcpy + extra writev increases syscalls and kills batching heuristics. Two options: normalize in-place (needs boundary checks) or build iov vec directly.

alex: prefer iov-direct approach. estimate low-risk patch: build iov by referencing slices of the original buffer, avoid extra allocation and memcpy. Jordan can you own prototype?

jordan: on it. I'll bench both approaches and submit PR with microbench numbers. ETA EOD tomorrow.

ria: also want a regression test: synthetic runner that exercises 20-100 token requests with grpc streaming enabled and measures writev count + host p50. I'll add that to the runtime perf CI.

tobias: one more note: check KV cache eviction patterns while testing. more writev could change queuing and affect kv cache prefetch timings (we saw small KV miss bump in one trace).

alex: great catch. assign tickets: RH-2357 proto iov-direct fix (jordan), RH-2358 perf-ci streaming writev test (ria), RH-2359 kv-cache followup (tobias).

jordan: thanks — will post bench diff here when I have it. :thumbsup:
